new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Only one work is listed and the reader opened it, so there were no listed silent or unopened works to spot-check. As a bonus I a full-text search for stress/accent the other saved (non-listed) files in the chon1248 folder for stress terms: Cooper 1917 (BAE Bulletin 63, the scanned text) has '(')= principal stress; (:)= secondary stress (Skottsberg, d, 606, 614)' but this is Skottsberg's phonetic alphabet for his Alacaluf (Kawesqar) vocabulary, not Chono; Ibar Bruce 1960 (the scanned textp. 61-70 article) says 'las voces chonas tomaron con el tiempo un acento español', i.e. Chono toponyms acquired a Hispanicised pronunciation, not a word-stress statement.
